clue.text: A band take endless trouble to provide a lot of information

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order
the word take loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, before its end is cut

explanation.surface: A group of musicians goes to great lengths to supply plenty of facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take endless trouble' reads as an idiom for making an effort, but it splits into fodder, a deletion and the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A databank is a large store of data held for consultation, a lot of information in one place.

clue.text: System for better transport

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the totalisator, a pool betting system used at racecourses; a better is one who bets
second meaning: to carry, as in toting a bag

explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like the comparative of good, but here it is someone who places bets.
explanation.definitionFit: The tote is the racecourse pool-betting system, and to tote is an informal verb for carrying something.

clue.text: A medical man in centre of capital

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside the word for centre

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor stands in the heart of a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Madrid is the capital city of Spain.

clue.text: Priest moved her chair

indicators.note: the letters of these two words are moved around into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A clergyman shifts a woman's seat out of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarch is a chief priest or senior religious leader who heads a hierarchy.

clue.text: Bill of Rights set out in Act (anagram)

indicators.note: to set something out is to lay it out afresh, so these letters are laid out in a new order

parts.note: the word itself, taken as written, is part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A charter of rights laid down in a statute, with a note that the clue is an anagram.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed '(anagram)' looks like an editor's label on the clue, but the word itself is fodder: its letters plus those of Act make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magna Carta of 1215 is the English charter limiting royal power, often called the first bill of rights.

clue.text: Fellow going to university, true to form, is tense

indicators.note: the word true is shaped into another form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man heading to university who is true to type turns out to be nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as an anxious adjective, but it is the grammatical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The future is a grammatical tense, used for events that have not happened yet.

clue.text: Damage to second boat affected by time

indicators.note: the word boat is affected, that is altered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A second vessel is harmed with the passing of the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate destruction or obstruction, damage done on purpose.

clue.text: He has a towering reputation in Paris

definitions.text: He has a towering reputation in Paris

parts.note: sounds like a man of great standing, but towering is literal: his name is on a tower
places the tower in the French capital

explanation.walkthrough: Gustave Eiffel's company built the tower that bears his name, so his fame literally towers over Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The engineer Gustave Eiffel is famous for the iron tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris.

clue.text: High flier, one taking vehicle to America

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: A successful person drives off to the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High flier' usually means an achiever; here it is literal, for the boy who flew too near the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew on wax wings so close to the sun that they melted.

clue.text: Time for fruit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a day or point in time, as on a calendar
second meaning: the sweet brown fruit of a palm

explanation.walkthrough: 'For' joins two separate meanings of the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: A date is a particular day, and it is also the fruit of the date palm.

clue.text: Vote for Red Rum: new fee arranged

indicators.note: the letters are arranged afresh into a new order

explanation.surface: A ballot on the famous racehorse Red Rum is set up for a new charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum was a celebrated British racehorse that won the Grand National three times.
explanation.definitionFit: A referendum is a direct vote by the whole electorate on a single question.

clue.text: Song and dance by a leading diva

parts.note: a ball is a formal dancing party

indicators.note: the leading part of the word diva is its opening letter

parts.note: the singer whose first letter is used

explanation.surface: A star singer leads off a song-and-dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' looks like the fixed phrase for a fuss, but it splits into the definition and a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a song, often one that tells a story or a slow sentimental number.

clue.text: They help one see long street differently

indicators.note: the letters of these words are set out differently

explanation.surface: Something lets you view a lengthy road in a new way.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorgnettes are spectacles held up to the eyes on a long handle, an aid to seeing.

clue.text: Increased the wealth of poor Cheri in the end

indicators.note: the jumbled name is placed in the word for the end
poor here means badly formed, so the name Cheri is rearranged

explanation.surface: Poor Cheri finally made somebody rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' sits beside a word about wealth, so it looks like part of the money story.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich someone is to make them richer, so the past tense means made wealthier.

clue.text: Take a right turn in self-defence

indicators.note: the letters are given a turn, mixing them into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions in a martial-arts lesson: turn right to protect yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese martial art of unarmed combat, taught as a method of self-defence.

clue.text: Last man I worked with had charm

indicators.note: these letters are worked into a new shape, as dough is worked

explanation.surface: My previous colleague was a charming fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' reads as personal appeal, but it is the lucky object.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object thought to bring good luck, a charm or amulet.

clue.text: Attack the accusation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to rush at an enemy

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one word sit side by side; 'the' only links them.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a headlong assault in battle, and also a formal accusation of an offence.

clue.text: Cecil retired abroad, which is thrilling

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters spread out into a new order

explanation.surface: Cecil has retired overseas, and life there is exciting.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric used figuratively means charged with excitement, like an electric atmosphere.

clue.text: Reach a swirling river

indicators.note: water swirling round churns the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting to an eddying stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive at a place is to reach it at the end of a journey.

clue.text: Caught dog trainer with dealer

parts.note: a handler trains and controls a dog, as police dog handlers do

explanation.surface: A man who trains dogs is caught along with a trader.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandler is a dealer in a particular trade, originally candles, now often ships' supplies.

clue.text: Fear at finding gold runs out in sixty minutes

indicators.note: the gold and runs go into the remaining letters of the hour
the U is taken out of the hour

explanation.surface: Panic at discovering the gold has run out within the hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' deletes the U from the hour without the U being separately clued, a loose touch of this setter's; R is the cricket abbreviation for runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Horror is intense fear mixed with shock or disgust.

clue.text: The back without exercise can come a cropper

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the rear goes outside the exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone with a bad back who skips exercise may take a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come a cropper' is the British idiom for falling heavily; here a cropper is literally one who crops.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaper cuts and gathers grain, so it crops the harvest: a cropper in the literal sense.

clue.text: Area, for example, in American state — nothing new!

indicators.note: the example goes inside the state

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A district, say, in a US state with nothing fresh about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A region is an area or district, a tract of land or part of a country.

clue.text: In favour of setting off and joining the demonstration

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: set off, the letters of setting go off into a new order

explanation.surface: A supporter sets off to march with the protesters.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesting means objecting in public, as marchers do when they join a demonstration.

clue.text: Bishop to come back and first help the two of them

indicators.note: the word to comes back, read in reverse
only the first letter of help is used

parts.note: the word whose opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A bishop returns and comes to help the pair of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both refers to two people or things together, the pair of them.

clue.text: Flog Ecstasy in club

indicators.note: the drug goes into the club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Selling drugs in a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' is British slang for sell and 'club' suggests a nightclub, but flog here means whip.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone is to strike them repeatedly, the same as flogging them.

clue.text: Chap, say, has a drink here

definitions.note: a place, not a noun meaning drink: where you drink

parts.note: bod is informal British for a person or chap
say signals an example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A fellow, let's say, orders a drink at this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or bar, a place where one goes to drink.

clue.text: Concerned with one form of madness

definitions.text: Concerned with one form of madness

parts.note: reads as being bothered by something, but the one is oneself
the suffix for obsession or mania

explanation.walkthrough: The ego is the self, so a mania for the ego is obsessive concern with one person: yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is an extreme, obsessive preoccupation with oneself, named like a mental disorder.
